sources.excerpt: All primary experiments start from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (Bai et al., 2025a) and train directly, without SFT warm-up, on a fixed set of 168,460 multiple-choice image–video examples from Video- R1-260k (Feng et al., 2025). Except in the training-step ablation, the training budget is 400 optimization steps. We post-train separate models with GRPO (Shao et al., 2024), SAPO (Gao et al., 2025), On-policy GKD (Agarwal et al., 2024), OPD (Lu & Lab, 2025), OPSD (Zhao et al., 2026b), RLSD (Yang et al., 2026b), RLCSD (Pan et al., 2026), and VAttnPO. Each method retains its original objective while sharing the training data, optimization budget, and evaluation protocol. GRPO and VAttnPO additionally share the verifiable reward, sampling, clipping, and KL regularization; their sole method difference is that VAttnPO replaces the broadcast sequence advantage with Equation (8).

Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027 et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025a), or read dense guidance from teacher- and privileged-context outputtoken distributions (Agarwal et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2026b; Pan et al., 2026). A vision-language model also produces attention over visual inputs at every generated token, providing an internal readout distinct from output behavior. We treat visual attention as a proxy to be evaluated through behavioral diagnostics and controlled training comparisons, rather than as a causal attribution or certificate of correctness (Liu et al., 2026; Zhao et al., 2026a; Lu et al., 2026; Yang et al., 2026a).
All benchmark evaluations use VLMEvalKit (Duan et al., 2026) and follow its default protocol for each benchmark, including prompting, decoding, answer extraction, and scoring.

We used generative AI tools to polish the writing, check mathematical derivations and formulas, and assist with writing and running parts of the research code, including submitting training jobs. The authors reviewed the edited text, verified the mathematical arguments, and inspected the AI-assisted code and resulting runs. We take full responsibility for the final manuscript and results.

Multimodal large language models are advancing rapidly, spanning tool-integrated reasoning, streaming perception, multi-image grounding, policy optimization, and large-scale evaluation (Chen et al., 2026b; Shen et al., 2026; Chen et al., 2026a; Zheng et al., 2026; Han et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2025). Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) uses automatic feedback, such as answer correctness and format compliance, to improve reasoning.

VAttnPO obtains the highest score among compared methods on all seven structured, document, and reliability metrics in Table 2. Its largest margins over GRPO are 2.21 points on HallusionBench aAcc and 1.64 on CountBenchQA (Beyer et al., 2024), whereas gains on document tasks are smaller, including 0.19 on DocVQA. The magnitudes are therefore heterogeneous, but their direction extends the improvement beyond the six image tasks to visual reliability, counting, and document understanding.

Question: During the IQ test, you'll be presented with existing picture example, and four picture options. Your task is to identify the one picture that follows the same pattern or rule established by the previous pictures. Here are some strategies to help you determine the right choice: 1. Look for patterns related to quantity or numbers that progress from one picture to the next. 2. Check if there is a consistent way the images are rotated or flipped in sequence.

Position-only replaces visual credit with a centered, RMScalibrated position curve; No position retains visual credit with uniform position weights; and the KL variant replaces JSD similarity with reference smoothing, forward KL, and an exponential map while retaining position modulation and credit balancing. Position-only reaches 70.84 AVE, close to GRPO at 70.97; No position reaches 72.35, and the full VAttnPO reaches 73.50. Visual credit therefore contributes beyond a positional prior, with position modulation providing a further gain. The KL variant reaches 71.37; this comparison concerns only the construction defined in Appendix F and leaves policy KL regularization unchanged.

sources.excerpt: Table F.2: Per-benchmark results for position and credit-balance variants. Variant

) and exceeds the strongest compared baseline, OPD at 71.27, by 2.23 points. All six image tasks improve over GRPO: the largest gains are 4.18 on VStar and 4.08 on MuirBench, while the other four tasks also remain positive. This distribution shows that the average gain spans both fine-grained perception and visual reasoning rather than being driven by one benchmark.

VAttnPO’s gains extend beyond the six image tasks. It improves all four video benchmarks over GRPO, by 0.90 on MVBench, 0.8 on LongVideoBench, and 1.54 on TempCompass, with a smaller margin of 0.2 on Video-MME. It also improves MME-per and MME-rea by 18.9 and 10.0 points, respectively (Table 3). Consequently, these performance improvements span short-form video, long-form video, temporal aspects, and other multimodal evaluations, with the magnitude of improvement varying across different benchmarks.

The main training data are cleaned multiple-choice samples selected from Video-R1-260k (Feng et al., 2025). All primary methods use the same frozen training manifest. The data-composition ablation changes only this manifest and leaves the other training settings unchanged. Table A.1: Training-set composition. Data type

Training uses ms-swift 4.4.1 with its default visual preprocessing and video-sampling settings, running on eight NVIDIA L20X GPUs with bfloat16 precision and DeepSpeed ZeRO-2. Except for the explicit checkpoint comparison, the main results use the prespecified 400-step endpoint rather than selecting checkpoints by test performance.

All three diagnostics use layer 20 of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and the same image-only candidate pool. The candidate record contains 10,199 responses to 1,485 prompts from the image distribution of the training set; 732 prompts contain both correct and incorrect responses. We sample 200 of these prompts without replacement using seed 42 and obtain 1,429 valid trajectories, comprising 771 correct and 658 incorrect responses. For correct–incorrect comparisons, responses are aggregated within each prompt before prompts receive equal weight. The 95% intervals use 2,000 bootstrap resamples with the prompt as the cluster unit.
